headline: Indian Markets Focus on Weekly Triggers as Bank Unions Defer Strike and Oil Concerns Persist

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: India shares logged their longest weekly losing run since 2020 as high oil prices weighed on sentiment.
Investors are closely watching market triggers including US yields, crude prices, and global geopolitics.
Union Minister Piyush Goyal is expected to meet USTR Jamieson Greer amid tariff threats.
Bank unions deferred a three-day nationwide strike after reaching an understanding with the IBA.
whatHappening: DGCA launched a probe into an IndiGo flight that suffered a tail strike during landing at Bengaluru.
Bank unions deferred their planned 3-day nationwide strike following assurances from the IBA.
NSE partnered with Augmont to expand the Electronic Gold Receipts market.
Nippon Express targets $380 million in revenue as India's semiconductor ecosystem expands.
summary: Indian equities enter the session after recording their longest weekly losing run since 2020 due to elevated oil prices. Bank unions have deferred a planned three-day strike following assurances from the IBA. Meanwhile, DGCA launched a probe into a tail strike incident involving an IndiGo flight in Bengaluru.
